claims.text: Severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in brittle intermetallic-containing high-entropy alloys.
The investigated material is CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2 with an FCC matrix containing complex Laves-phase particles.
The intervention consists of severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h and rolled to a 90% thickness reduction, producing a final thickness of about 0.4 mm.
Cryo-rolling involved immersion in liquid nitrogen for 0.5 h before and after every pass.
Rolled material was annealed at 800 °C for 1 h and then water quenched.
Cryo-rolling and annealing produce a heterogeneous microstructure containing coexisting deformed and recrystallized regions.
Cryo-rolling creates a greater density of precipitation nucleation sites, including dislocations, shear bands, and grain boundaries.
The greater density of nucleation sites accelerates nanosized ε-phase precipitation early during recrystallization.
The nanosized ε-phase precipitates pin high-angle boundaries through Zener pinning.
Zener pinning inhibits recrystallization and thereby creates a mixture of deformed and recrystallized regions.
Mechanical incompatibility between deformed and recrystallized domains generates strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations.
The strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations create long-range back stress.
Long-range back stress delays necking and enhances both strength and ductility.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has a yield strength of 1219 ± 14 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has an ultimate tensile strength of 1272 ± 25 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has approximately 22% elongation.
The cold-rolled and annealed baseline has a yield strength of 774 ± 13 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 1085 ± 18 MPa, and approximately 20% elongation.
Cryo-rolling and annealing increase yield strength by about 400 MPa, or about 58%, relative to cold-rolling and annealing.
The study did not quantify the back stress generated by the heterogeneous microstructure.
